Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest

Class GameTestScaffold

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.GameTestScaffold
public final class GameTestScaffold extends Object
Scaffolding shared by each loader's GameTests: placing each stack type on the empty template through CommonRegistry, seeding handlers directly, and the assertion helpers every test reads through. Loader-native automation access stays in Forge's and NeoForge's GameTestSupport and Fabric's FabricGameTestSupport.

Seeding writes to a handler rather than going through a deposit, so a test can build a state the ordinary rules would not produce and check what happens next.

    • seedSlot

      public static void seedSlot(com.github.crittscott.somestacks.util.StackItemStorage handler, int slot, net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack)
      Puts stack straight into a slot, bypassing the validity test an insertion runs.

      This is how a test reaches the state an ss deny mod edit or a data pack reload leaves behind: contents a block holds and must keep handing back, which that same block would refuse from a deposit today. Validity gates insertion only, so the stored side of that rule has to be set up without going through insertion. StorageStackBE.setSlotIfChanged(int, net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack) takes the same route for the same reason.

    • heldAt

      public static int heldAt(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos absolutePos, net.minecraft.world.item.Item item)
      Items of item still held by the stack block at absolutePos. A position the block has removed itself from holds none, which is what a caller counting whether an operation conserved its contents wants to see.
